query: Which material can be used for improve the magnetocaloric properties, and why?

generation.hypothesis: Doping existing magnetocaloric materials with rare earth elements, specifically Gadolinium (Gd), will improve their magnetocaloric properties.
generation.material_initial_state: Existing magnetocaloric materials with limited properties, such as Gd5Si2Ge2
generation.intervention: Doping with 5% atomic concentration of Gd
generation.conditions: Near room temperature (300 K) and in a magnetic field of 2 Tesla
generation.structural_mediator: Modification of the crystal structure and magnetic exchange interactions
generation.mechanism: The introduction of Gd ions alters the magnetic ordering and enhances the magnetocaloric effect through increased magnetic entropy change
generation.predicted_outcome: An increase in the isothermal entropy change (ΔS) of 20% relative to the undoped material
generation.boundary: Magnetic field range: 0-5 Tesla, Temperature range: 250-350 K
generation.uncertainty: The actual improvement in magnetocaloric properties may vary depending on the specific material and doping concentration, and the rare earth element used for doping may affect the outcome

falsification_experiment.design: Measure the isothermal entropy change (ΔS) of doped and undoped samples using magnetization measurements
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the measured ΔS of the doped sample is not at least 15% higher than that of the undoped sample, the hypothesis is falsified

limitation.current limitation: limited magnetocaloric properties in existing materials
